system_line: Answer the question you are given.
changed_rule: An answer counts as changed when its text differs from the same model's previous recorded answer to the same question, after Unicode NFKC, case-folding, collapsing whitespace and stripping punctuation and quotes at both ends. It is a plain text comparison and says nothing about which answer is right.

groups.name: Health and home
groups.why: General knowledge a person might ask at home. Nothing that asks for a diagnosis.

groups.name: Right now
groups.why: Answers that should move as time passes.

groups.name: About the AI
groups.why: What the model says it is and can do.

questions.text: How many days are in a year?
questions.rationale: About as simple as a question gets, with a small catch: leap years. It shows whether a model gives the short answer, the careful one, or both, and whether that habit shifts.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

How many days are in a year?

questions.text: How many minutes are in a day?
questions.rationale: A one-step sum with a single right number. If this answer ever changes, something other than the facts has changed.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

How many minutes are in a day?

questions.text: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.rationale: A fact people often get wrong by guessing the largest city. The answer should stay the same for as long as the archive runs.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

What is the capital of Australia?

questions.text: How many continents are there?
questions.rationale: Usually taught as seven, but other counts are used in some places. It shows whether a model states one number or mentions the others.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

How many continents are there?

questions.text: At what temperature does water boil, in Celsius?
questions.rationale: A school fact with a condition attached: the pressure. It shows whether the condition is mentioned without being asked for.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

At what temperature does water boil, in Celsius?

questions.text: How much water does an adult need to drink in a day?
questions.rationale: Common advice has changed over the years and depends on the person. This records which figure a model reaches for and how firmly it states it.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

How much water does an adult need to drink in a day?

questions.text: How many hours of sleep does an adult need?
questions.rationale: General guidance that most people have heard. The range a model gives, and whether it adds a caveat, can drift between versions.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

How many hours of sleep does an adult need?

questions.text: How long does it take to wash your hands properly?
questions.rationale: A short public-health rule of thumb. It should be stable, which makes any change easy to see.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

How long does it take to wash your hands properly?

questions.text: How long can cooked rice be kept in the fridge?

questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

How long can cooked rice be kept in the fridge?

questions.text: What temperature should a fridge be set to, in Celsius?
questions.rationale: A household setting with a commonly quoted range. Useful as a steady reference next to questions that move.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

What temperature should a fridge be set to, in Celsius?

questions.text: What is today's date?
questions.rationale: A model has no clock. This question shows whether it says so, guesses from its training, or reads the date from what it was given, and whether that habit shifts between versions.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

What is today's date?

questions.text: What year is it?
questions.rationale: The same problem as the date, in its shortest form. A guess here moves forward as newer models are trained on newer text.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

What year is it?

questions.text: What is the newest phone you know about?
questions.rationale: Phones are released every year, so the answer dates the model's knowledge in a way most people can check for themselves.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

What is the newest phone you know about?

questions.text: What is the tallest building in the world?
questions.rationale: True for years at a time, then suddenly out of date. It shows how long an old answer keeps being repeated after the world has moved.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

What is the tallest building in the world?

questions.text: What is the most recent news event you know about?
questions.rationale: An open question about where a model's knowledge stops. The answer is expected to change with every new model version.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

What is the most recent news event you know about?

questions.text: Which model are you, and who made you?
questions.rationale: The name a model gives for itself can be compared with the model ID the answer was recorded under. They do not always agree.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

Which model are you, and who made you?

questions.text: Can you look things up while answering this?
questions.rationale: In this archive the model is sent the question on its own, with no tools. This records whether it describes that correctly.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

Can you look things up while answering this?

questions.text: What is your knowledge cutoff date?
questions.rationale: Models are often unsure of their own cutoff. The stated date can be set beside the answers in the group above.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

What is your knowledge cutoff date?

questions.text: Will you remember this conversation tomorrow?
questions.rationale: Here each question is a separate request and nothing is kept between them. This records what the model says about that.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

Will you remember this conversation tomorrow?

questions.text: What kind of question are you most likely to get wrong?
questions.rationale: A model's own account of its weak spots, kept so that it can be compared across versions. It is a statement, not a measurement.
questions.prompt:
Answer in one or two sentences.

What kind of question are you most likely to get wrong?
